h2: Eddy current testing in Detroit: sorting, coating checks and tube inspection windows
html:
Eddy current testing in Detroit: sorting, coating checks and tube inspection windows

In metro Detroit, eddy current testing does three main jobs: sorting and verifying parts in manufacturing, measuring coatings and conductivity on aluminum and other metals, and testing heat-exchanger, condenser and chiller tubes while the equipment is offline. Atlantis sends ET technicians from Houston for site work, with procedures reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III, and also runs ET training for technicians.

Sorting and material checks. Eddy current responds to conductivity, permeability and geometry, so it can separate mixed stock, flag parts that missed heat treatment, and confirm the temper of aluminum castings and extrusions through conductivity readings in %IACS. The method is comparative: the setup is only as good as the reference parts of known good and known bad condition it is balanced on, and those references must be kept and re-verified. When a specification asks for an actual hardness number or a confirmed alloy grade, ET is a screen, not the answer. Atlantis offers hardness testing and positive material identification for those cases.

Coatings. Eddy current gauges measure nonconductive coatings such as paint and anodize on nonferrous metals, while magnetic gauges handle coatings on steel; ASTM D7091 covers both. On painted structures, eddy current can also find cracks at weld toes without stripping the coating, provided the coating is thin and its thickness is known, because lift-off changes the signal.

Tube inspection windows. Michigan's long heating season leaves comfort-cooling chillers idle for months, and that is when their bundles are opened, cleaned and tested. Refinery and power plant exchangers are tested during planned outages. Non-ferrous chiller tubes are normally screened with a bobbin probe, while steel tubes call for a ferromagnetic technique or IRIS ultrasonic tube inspection. Ask for a tube map and the raw data, not only a count of plugged tubes, so the next campaign can be compared tube by tube.

  • Conductivity checks on aluminum castings and extrusions
  • Comparative sorting of fasteners, shafts and heat-treated parts
  • Crack detection at weld toes and edges through thin coatings
  • Bobbin, array and rotating-probe examination of exchanger and chiller tubing

Site rules. Michigan runs its own OSHA-approved State Plan, so the state's rules apply to confined-space entry into exchanger channel heads and to lockout during tube work. Where the equipment is a boiler, the Boiler Division of the Bureau of Construction Codes within the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs is the state authority, and tube findings go into the record the boiler inspector sees.

What ET can and cannot detect is set out on the eddy current testing page; plant-wide scopes begin at NDT inspection services. Technicians can take ET training, practice signal reading on the Practical NDT eddy current simulator, and enroll locally through the Detroit NDT training page. To scope a job, send the part or tube details, quantities and access window through the Detroit ET request.
